sources.content_summary: Tauri mobile apps compile the application as a library and load the function marked with mobile_entry_point through the platform framework.
key_points: The app crate needs staticlib, cdylib, and rlib outputs.
The mobile entry point belongs in src/lib.rs.
tauri.conf.json identifies the Tauri project to the CLI.
misconceptions: A test-only rlib with no mobile entry point is a runnable mobile application.

sources.content_summary: A mobile plugin call crosses Rust PluginHandle into an annotated Kotlin command on Android or an Objective-C-visible Swift function on iOS.
key_points: Android plugins extend Plugin and use TauriPlugin and Command annotations.
iOS plugins extend Plugin and expose Invoke functions.
Rust calls native code with run_mobile_plugin.
misconceptions: Desktop MockRuntime execution proves Kotlin or Swift execution.

sources.content_summary: Capabilities grant plugin commands to named windows; multiple matching capabilities merge their permissions.
key_points: The mobile main window needs an explicit plugin permission.
Allowed and denied evidence must not attach both capabilities to the same window in one build.
A separate configuration selection can produce a genuine denial run.
misconceptions: Adding an empty denial capability cancels an allow capability on the same window.

sources.content_summary: The supported Tauri 2 workflow installs the CLI and initializes Android/iOS targets from a complete app project.
key_points: The repository may use pnpm for a JS CLI or cargo-tauri.
android init and ios init generate platform projects.
android dev/run and ios dev/run execute on targets.
misconceptions: Native plugin source trees alone are sufficient for target execution receipts.

sources.content_summary: The maintained Tauri 2 base template uses a three-crate-type library, mobile_entry_point, Builder registration, and a tiny desktop main delegating to run.
key_points: Follow the complete maintained template shape.
Use static frontend assets for the narrow certification screen.
misconceptions: A mobile target can be added by changing only tauri.conf.json.
